svg.text: The two components that decide whether the water in the tank is safe. Scale 1:50 / 1:10 as noted.
Peak flow at 180 mm/h design intensity = 0.80 L/s → 75 mm gutter, 50 mm downpipe for a 20 m² roof.
Gutter fall must be at least 1:200 towards the downpipe. A gutter that ponds is a mosquito breeding site.
Sizing basis: Rational Method at 180 mm/h design intensity (1:25-yr, 10-min storm, Bangladesh).
Gutter capacity from Manning at 1:200 fall, n = 0.011, flowing full.
Never downsize a downpipe to save a fitting: the gutter will overtop at the wall and wash out the footing.
THE THREE RULES THAT DECIDE WATER QUALITY
1. Keep the first 1.5 mm out of the tank.
It carries most of the faecal indicator bacteria and the
leaf-derived colour. This is the single highest-value
component in the whole system for its cost.
An uncovered tank grows algae and breeds Aedes
mosquitoes. A sealed, lockable cover is not optional.
Draw through a tap, never a bucket on a rope. A rope
dipped into the tank is the fastest route to contamination.
Water fills the chamber first. The float rises and seals the outlet,
so the dirtiest first water is trapped instead of entering the tank.
A 3 mm bleed hole drains it over 10–15 min, the float drops, and the
diverter re-arms itself for the next rain event. No manual reset.
Discard volume = 1.5 mm × catchment area: T1 30 L T2 180 L T3 600 L
Replace the charcoal and the top 50 mm of sand every 6 months.
Backwash monthly: open the drain, run 10 L to waste.
A filter that is never cleaned becomes a bacterial incubator — worse than no filter.
